title: Consumption Safeguard Playbook for QBRs
content:
Purpose:
Provide a compact, repeatable worksheet and response playbook to use during quarterly business reviews (QBRs) that focuses on short-term consumption anomalies, token spend controls, rate-limit incidents, and budget alert tuning. This doc is intended for CS RMs preparing QBR decks and on-call engineers who need clear, actionable remediation steps during a customer billing or rate-limit surprise.

Context and assumptions:
- Customers using a mix of hosted API and Dedicated pools. Data pulled from billing exports, request logs, and the token-metering pipeline (etl:billing_tokens_daily).
- We assume a 30/90/365 view: 30-day recent change, 90-day trend for seasonality, 365-day for renewal signals.
- This worksheet is lightweight and intentionally recommends conservative thresholds for early warning rather than reactive throttles.

Executive summary template (for QBR slides):
- Headline: "Usage growth + 7-day spikes driven by X task = projected +24% monthly spend"
- Immediate action: "Enabled temporary rate cap (50 RPS) + customer notified. Investigating retry storm from SDK v1.9.2"
- Renewal implication: "Low-medium risk; propose 3-month commit adjustment + dev assist on batching"

Key metrics to pull for the worksheet:
- tokens_total (30d, 90d, YoY)
- avg_tokens_per_request (median, 95p)
- requests_per_minute (p95)
- rate_limit_violations (count, unique endpoints/users)
- budget_alerts_triggered (count, severity)
- charged_overages (currency)

Quick data pulls (examples - run in BigQuery or billing UI):
- 30d tokens: SELECT SUM(tokens) FROM etl.billing_tokens_daily WHERE customer_id = 'CUST123' AND date >= DATE_SUB(CURRENT_DATE(), INTERVAL 30 DAY)
- Top endpoints by tokens: SELECT endpoint, SUM(tokens) FROM requests WHERE customer_id='CUST123' GROUP BY endpoint ORDER BY SUM(tokens) DESC LIMIT 10
- Rate-limit spikes: SELECT date_hour, COUNT(*) AS violations FROM rate_limit_events WHERE customer_id='CUST123' GROUP BY date_hour ORDER BY violations DESC LIMIT 24

Patterns and what they usually mean (heuristic):
- Gradual 20–40% 30d uptick with flat 95p latency: organic feature adoption; low churn risk, suggest commit-tier discussion.
- Sharp >100% 7d spike concentrated to a single endpoint: likely a runaway batch job or misconfigured cron; high short-term cost risk. Immediate rate cap + contact dev.
- Rising avg_tokens_per_request (median up) without request count growth: prompts have been changed; quality/regression risk. Recommend evals and batching suggestions.
- Frequent rate_limit_violations spread across endpoints: bot traffic or parallelization misuse; propose client-side backoff and server-side soft-bulkhead rules.

Suggested alert thresholds (starting recommendations):
- Token burn alert (P2): 30d tokens exceed forecasted baseline +25% (notify RM and billing).
- Burst alert (P1): any hour with tokens > 5x rolling 7-day hourly average or requests_per_minute > 200% p95 => immediate page to ops.
- Rate-limit trend (P2): rate_limit_violations > 50 in 24h OR > 10 unique endpoints hitting limits => notify RM and eskalate to eng if persistent.
- Budget alert (customer-managed budgets): 80% notify, 95% mandatory pre-commit notification and recommended temporary throttles.

Triage playbook (on-call / CS ops):
1) Verify data: Pull raw request logs for the incident window; check billing pipeline for late arrivals.
2) Identify scope: single API key / org-wide / single endpoint? Use query: SELECT DISTINCT api_key, endpoint FROM requests WHERE customer_id='CUST123' AND timestamp BETWEEN X AND Y
3) Apply temporary mitigation: apply a per-key rate cap or set per-route max_tokens override in the console to limit spend. Note: prefer short windows (1–4 hours) and inform RM.
4) Customer comms template (short): "Hi <name>, we detected an unexpected burst in usage impacting your monthly spend. We've applied a short, temporary rate cap while we investigate. Can you confirm any recent deploys or new integrations?"
5) Root cause and follow-up: if caused by SDK or integration bug, create JIRA and set follow-up with solutions engineering for batching/quantization recommendations.

QBR diagnostics checklist (fillable items for the meeting):
- 30d tokens, 90d trend, YoY comparison
- Top 3 endpoints contributing to incremental tokens
- Number of API keys with >10% change in per-key burn
- Any billing anomalies (late pipeline, duplicate charges)
- Recommended immediate action taken (rate cap, refund, credit, commit proposal)

Renewal signal scoring (simple 0–5):
- 0: Stable usage consistent with plan, no alerts last 90d
- 1–2: Minor volatility or one-off overage; RM contact and small commit suggestion
- 3: Repeated spikes or growing avg_tokens_per_request; schedule Solutions Eng review pre-renewal
- 4–5: Persistent overages, unhappy due to cost surprises; recommend alternate pricing conversation or dedicated capacity migration plan

Playbook snippets for cost mitigation recommendations (to include in QBR):
- Short-term: Apply per-key caps, enable response streaming size limits, reduce max_tokens on generation routes by 20%.
- Mid-term: Implement prefix caching for chat sessions, enable KV cache reuse, reduce redundant calls from orchestration layer.
- Long-term: Move predictable high-throughput workloads to Dedicated with reserved capacity and predictable unit economics.

Communication templates (for RM to include in QBR notes):
- Incident summary: "On 2026-02-14 we observed a 3x hourly token spike caused by a third-party batch job. We applied a temporary cap and issued a reversal for the excess charge. Recommended next step: set a daily budget alert and schedule a dev sync."
- Renewal prompt (if relevant): "We recommend an updated 3-month committed tier aligned to baseline+15% to avoid reoccurrence while engineering implements batching improvements."

Appendix: example console checks and internal links:
- Billing export (console): /billing/customers/CUST123/exports
- Token meter health dashboard: console.redwood.ai/dashboards/token-meter
- Related runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/CS/SOS-Billing-Runbook

Open questions and TODOs for this doc (for the team):
- Add a compact spreadsheet template with auto-calculated forecast deltas (owner: Ravi).
- Integrate a sample Prometheus alert for the burst rule into SRE repo (owner: Evan).
- Run a small experiment on auto-soft-throttles for SDK v1.9 clients and capture false-positive rate (owner: Maya).

Notes to self (scratch):
- Keep the worksheet tight — customers appreciate one-slide, three-action summaries.
- Avoid deep product language in customer-facing templates; focus on impact and next steps.

End of document.
